mixing_sequence: Fill reservoir tank with RO or filtered water (< 100 ppm TDS)
Dissolve Calcium Nitrate Ca(NO3)2 — stir 2 mins until fully dissolved
Dissolve NPK Grow/Bloom Base — stir 2 mins until solution is clear
Dissolve Epsom Salt MgSO4 — stir 2 mins
Wait 15 minutes for chemical stabilization
Measure pH and EC with digital pen
Adjust pH drop-by-drop with pH Down — lock to target 5.8–6.2
critical_rules: Never mix dry powders together — dissolve each separately in 1L warm water first
Always add Calcium Nitrate FIRST before any other nutrient
Always adjust pH LAST after all salts are dissolved
Outdoor: top up with plain pH 6.0 water mid-week; full drain every 14 days

phases.name: Seedling & Transplant
daily_tasks: Verify drip stake water flow (15m ON / 60m OFF)
Ensure drain line flows freely without back-pooling
weekly_tasks: Test pH/EC every 3 days; adjust with pH Down if pH > 6.0
Drain reservoir & refill with Phase 2 mix at end of W2
observations: White root tips emerging through perlite base
Leaves bright green without tip scorching
Stem diameter reaching 4–5 mm

phases.name: Early Vegetative
daily_tasks: Top up reservoir with plain pH 6.0 water daily
Check LED grow light height (14"–16" above canopy)
weekly_tasks: Pinch Crown Bud: remove single flower at first Y-fork
Strip suckers — prune all side shoots below first Y-fork
Tie main trunk to bamboo stake
observations: Stem thickens into woody structure
Clear Y-fork branching pattern establishes
Vigorous white root growth in siphon elbow zone

phases.name: Late Vegetative
daily_tasks: Verify daytime circulation fan movement (leaves should gently dance)
Check reservoir water temp (< 24°C)
weekly_tasks: Select 2–3 main leaders; prune weak inward shoots
Strip leaves lower 5" off perlite for air circulation
Drain reservoir & refill Phase 4 mix at end of W6
observations: Lush dark green leaf canopy
Absence of yellowing lower leaves
Branch cell walls thickening to support fruit weight

phases.name: Pre-Flowering Transition
daily_tasks: Inspect branch nodes for tight flower bud clusters
Monitor water consumption (uptake accelerates)
weekly_tasks: Install vertical nylon trellis strings to overhead wire
Twist main leaders around trellis cords
Thin double flower clusters down to 1 strong bud per node
observations: Abundant flower bud formation
Plant height reaching 2.5–3.0 feet
Stem nodes tightening

phases.name: Flowering & Fruit Set
daily_tasks: Hand Pollinate (Indoor): swirl artist brush inside flowers 10 AM–2 PM daily
Monitor temp (21°C–29°C; avoid > 32°C)
weekly_tasks: Lock pH strictly to 6.0–6.2 to enable calcium absorption
Full reservoir drain & fresh Phase 5 remix every 14 days
Clean pump intake sponge filter
observations: White petals dropping cleanly to reveal green pea-sized fruitlets
No blossom drop (flowers staying attached to stem)

phases.name: Peak Fruiting & Harvest
daily_tasks: Top up 2.5–4L water/bucket daily
Inspect fruit bottoms for Blossom-End Rot (dark leathery patches)
weekly_tasks: Harvest glossy green peppers weekly (leave 0.5" stem)
Clip heavy branches to trellis wires to prevent snapping
Full reservoir drain & remix every 14 days
observations: Thick-walled 3-to-4-lobed glossy peppers
Continuous waves of new blossoms at upper nodes
Leaves remain deep green without chlorosis

phases.name: Late Harvest
daily_tasks: Monitor fruit color shift from green to deep red/yellow
Top up water every 2 days
weekly_tasks: Snip main growing tips 4 weeks prior to end
Pinch all tiny new flower buds to channel energy into ripening
observations: 80%+ of fruit fully turned vibrant red or yellow
Sugar content peaking (sweet aroma)
Growth stalling naturally

phases.name: Final Flush
daily_tasks: Run plain pH 6.0 water (zero nutrients) for 7 days
weekly_tasks: Harvest final full crop on Day 7
Sterilize buckets & perlite with 3% H2O2 for next cycle
observations: Salts flushed out for crisp sweet pepper flavor
Roots turning tan prior to system shutdown

mixing_sequence: Fill UPVC pipe / container with fresh water
Dissolve Calcium Nitrate Ca(NO3)2 — stir until clear
Dissolve NPK Grow Base — stir 2 mins
Dissolve Epsom Salt MgSO4 — stir 2 mins
Wait 10 minutes for stabilization
Measure pH and EC with digital pen
Adjust pH with pH Down to target 5.5–6.5
critical_rules: Kratky system is passive — do NOT refill reservoir until it drops 30%
Maintain 1.5"–2" air gap between water surface and net cup bottom
Lower water level by 1 inch once roots hit water to create passive air gap

phases.name: Germination & Air Gap
daily_tasks: Verify net cup bottoms touch water level by 1/4 inch
Ensure indoor grow light runs 14 hrs/day
weekly_tasks: Check root emergence through net cup slots
Lower water level by 1 inch once roots hit water to create passive air gap
observations: White taproots protruding from coir plugs
Cotyledon leaves fully expanded

phases.name: Active Leaf Growth
daily_tasks: Check air-gap zone (roots must have 1.5"–2" air space above water)
Verify water temp stays below 25°C
weekly_tasks: Measure pH & EC; top up plain pH 6.0 water if solution drops > 30%
Inspect under leaves for aphids or leaf miners
observations: Rapid expansion of broad crinkled dark-green leaves
Healthy oxygenated white root mass suspended in air gap

phases.name: Pre-Harvest
daily_tasks: Check for early signs of bolting (center stem elongation)
Verify light distance (6" above leaves)
weekly_tasks: Harvest outer mature leaves weekly (cut-and-come-again method)
Full reservoir drain and reset after 30–35 days
observations: Tender vibrant green leaves ready for culinary picking
Absence of bitterness or tall flower stalks

phases.name: Nursery Plug
daily_tasks: Keep nursery sponge plugs damp
Ensure 16 hrs LED light exposure
weekly_tasks: Transfer seedlings with 3 true leaves into NFT/DWC net cups
Set initial low-strength Phase 1 nutrient mix
observations: Sturdy 3-to-4 leaf seedlings
Bright white root tips extending past sponge base

phases.name: Channel Growth
daily_tasks: Inspect NFT channel water flow (thin continuous film — no overflow)
Ensure circulation fan prevents Tip Burn
weekly_tasks: Check EC/pH twice weekly
Clean inline pump filter mesh
Check water temperature (< 24°C)
observations: Rapid leaf rosette expansion
Crisp clean leaf margins without brown tip burn
Abundant white root mats inside NFT channels

phases.name: Head Sizing & Harvest
daily_tasks: Inspect head firmness and weight
Check for root rot (browning/slimy roots)
weekly_tasks: Drain tank and run plain water flush for 48 hours prior to harvest
Harvest full intact head by cutting base stem at net cup
observations: Dense tightly cupped heads (180g–220g weight)
Sweet crisp flavor without bitter latex sap

Vibrate flower trusses daily at noon to release pollen (indoor)
Prune suckers weekly — snap off all side shoots growing in leaf axils
Full tank drain every 14 days during heavy fruiting phase

phases.name: Seedling
daily_tasks: Check drip emitters for steady drip flow
Verify daytime pump cycle (15m ON / 45m OFF)
weekly_tasks: Test pH/EC every 3 days
Stake seedling with plant clip
observations: Strong central stem
Deep green compound leaves without purple nitrogen-deficiency tint

phases.name: Early Vegetative
daily_tasks: Top up water reservoir daily
Check LED light distance (18" above top growth)
weekly_tasks: Prune Suckers: snap off all side shoots growing in leaf axils weekly
Wind main vine around vertical rollerhook twine
observations: Thick main stem (> 10mm diameter)
First flower truss emerging at node 7–8

phases.name: Flowering & Trusses
daily_tasks: Vibrate Trusses: tap flower clusters or vibrate with toothbrush at noon daily
Check room exhaust fan
weekly_tasks: Maintain EC at 2.2–2.5
Full tank drain & remix every 14 days
Prune lower leaves below lowest fruiting truss
observations: Bright yellow flower clusters setting into firm green cherry fruitlets
10–15 tomatoes per cluster truss

phases.name: Heavy Fruiting
daily_tasks: Top up 3–4L water/bucket daily
Inspect for Blossom-End Rot or fruit cracking
weekly_tasks: Harvest clusters of deep red glossy cherry tomatoes twice weekly
Continue sucker pruning and vertical cord winding
Full reservoir drain every 14 days
observations: Continuous waves of sweet high-Brix red cherry tomatoes
Strong vine reaching 6–8 feet height

phases.name: Ripening & Termination
daily_tasks: Top main growing tip 4 weeks prior to end
Reduce EC strength to 1.4 mS/cm
weekly_tasks: Pick final ripening fruit
Flush system with plain pH 6.0 water for 5 days before clearing vines

Clean final harvest yield

mixing_sequence: No liquid nutrients required — substrate provides all nutrition
Soak chopped wheat/paddy straw in clean water for 12 hours (target 65% moisture)
Mix 10 kg Wheat Bran + 2 kg Gypsum CaSO4 + 1 kg Calcium Carbonate per 100 kg straw
Hot water pasteurize at 65°C–70°C for 2 hours with 50g Bavistin per 100L water
Cool to room temperature before inoculation
Layer 5 kg Oyster Grain Spawn (5% spawn rate) into 50 PP bags under sterile conditions
critical_rules: Incubation must be in complete darkness — no light during spawn run
Do NOT run humidifier or exhaust fan during spawn run (Days 1–18)
Discard infected bags (green mold) immediately — do not delay
CO2 must stay below 800 ppm during fruiting — exhaust fan is mandatory

phases.name: Incubation / Spawn Run
daily_tasks: Keep incubation room in complete darkness
Monitor room temperature (24°C–26°C)
Do NOT run humidifier or exhaust fan during spawn run
weekly_tasks: Inspect all bags for Green Mold (Trichoderma) or black spots
Discard infected bags immediately out of room
Mop floor with 1% bleach solution
observations: White cottony mycelium running rapidly through straw substrate
Bag turning completely white by Day 15–18
Fresh mushroom aroma (no sour odor)

phases.name: Pinning & Fruiting
daily_tasks: Turn ON 4L Humidifier: maintain 85%–90% RH
Turn ON 200mm Exhaust Fan: keep CO2 < 800 ppm
Provide 10–12 hrs indirect light (1000 Lux)
Cut 4-5 X-shaped slits on bag walls
weekly_tasks: Harvest mature clusters by twisting base cleanly when cap edges uncurl
Mist room walls 3x daily
Allow bag 5-day resting period before Flush 2
observations: Tiny brown/gray pinhead clusters bursting out of bag slits by Day 20–22
Pinheads expanding into broad fan-shaped caps within 48–72 hours
Short stout stems with firm caps (good airflow indicator)

mixing_sequence: No liquid nutrients required — compost substrate provides all nutrition
Compost per 100 kg: 100 kg Wheat Straw + 60 kg Poultry Manure + 3 kg Urea + 15 kg Wheat Bran + 10 kg Gypsum
Pasteurize compost at 60°C–65°C
Casing soil at Day 18: mix 1 part Cow Dung + 1 part Coir Pith + 5% Chalk Powder CaCO3
Pasteurize casing soil at 65°C for 4 hours
Apply 1.5 inch casing layer over colonized compost
critical_rules: Temperature shock is mandatory: drop to 14°C–16°C at Day 26 to trigger pinning
Casing moisture should feel like a damp sponge — never muddy
Fill stem holes after each flush with fresh pasteurized casing soil
CO2 must stay below 1000 ppm during fruiting phase

phases.name: Spawn Run
daily_tasks: Maintain room temp at 23°C–25°C
Keep room pitch dark (0 Lux)
Keep humidity at 65%–70%
weekly_tasks: Inspect compost for uniform white mycelium thread colonization
Check for competitor molds (Aspergillus/Penicillium)
observations: Silvery-white mycelial threads spreading through dark compost
Full colonization by Day 15–17

phases.name: Casing & Case Run
daily_tasks: Apply pasteurized casing soil 1.5" deep over compost
Lightly mist casing layer with fine water spray
Maintain temp at 22°C–24°C
weekly_tasks: Check casing moisture (damp sponge feel — never muddy)
Mop room floor with 1% formalin solution
observations: Mycelium growing upward into casing layer
Case Run complete when white mycelium covers 70% of casing surface

phases.name: Temperature Shock & Pinning
daily_tasks: Cold Shock: drop AC temp strictly to 14°C–16°C
Increase fresh air ventilation (CO2 < 1000 ppm)
Turn ON Humidifier (85%–90% RH)
weekly_tasks: Inspect casing surface for tiny white pinhead initials
Maintain gentle surface misting
observations: Mycelium knotting into tiny pea-sized white button pins
Pins developing smooth round cap shapes

phases.name: Harvesting & Flushes
daily_tasks: Harvest solid tight white button caps by twisting gently at base
Keep room temp at 16°C–18°C
weekly_tasks: Fill stem holes in casing with fresh pasteurized casing soil
Water casing lightly after clearing Flush 1 to trigger Flush 2
observations: Clean bright-white button mushrooms (30mm–50mm cap diameter) with veil intact
3 successive harvest flushes spaced 7 days apart
